answer: A luthier workshop record with instrument serial registry works as the gate: instruments built and registered under one maker for years. Each of 107 aliases needs its own serial registries, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The saffron test is the price tag: 107 fakes mean 107 payments. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The jetty signal is visible to every grader, and the jade ledger is what makes the farm's arithmetic fail.
